title: Hosea Chapter 8 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Hosea chapter 8 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Hosea Chapter 8 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Hosea Chapter 8.

questions.question: According to Hosea 8:1, what instrument is set to the mouth as a warning?
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:1 states, 'Set the trumpet to thy mouth.' This indicates the use of a trumpet as a warning instrument.

questions.question: Who is described as coming against the house of the LORD like an eagle in Hosea 8?
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:1 says, 'He shall come as an eagle against the house of the LORD,' referring to a coming judgment.

questions.question: What reason does Hosea give for the eagle coming against the house of the LORD?
options: They have transgressed my covenant and trespassed against my law
They have prospered in their land
questions.correctAnswer: They have transgressed my covenant and trespassed against my law
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:1 explains the eagle comes because 'they have transgressed my covenant, and trespassed against my law.'

questions.question: What does Israel cry unto God according to Hosea 8:2?
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:2 records Israel crying out, 'My God, we know thee,' showing a claim of recognition.

questions.question: According to Hosea 8:3, what has Israel cast off?
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:3 says, 'Israel hath cast off the thing that is good,' indicating rejection of good.

questions.question: What consequence does Hosea 8:3 say will come upon Israel for casting off the good?
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:3 states, 'the enemy shall pursue him' as a consequence for Israel's rejection.

questions.question: Who have they set up that was not by God, according to Hosea 8:4?
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:4 says, 'They have set up kings, but not by me,' indicating kings chosen without God's approval.

questions.question: What have they made from silver and gold, according to Hosea 8:4?
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:4 states they made idols from silver and gold, which led to their downfall.

questions.question: In Hosea 8:5, what is the calf of Samaria said to have done?
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:5 says, 'Thy calf, O Samaria, hath cast thee off,' indicating rejection by the idol.

questions.question: What emotion is kindled against them in Hosea 8:5?
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:5 states, 'mine anger is kindled against them,' showing God's displeasure.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 8:6 says the calf of Samaria was made by a workman and is therefore God.
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:6 says the calf was made by a workman and 'therefore it is not God,' so the statement is false.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 8:7 teaches that sowing the wind results in reaping the whirlwind.
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:7 states, 'For they have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind,' affirming this truth.

questions.question: According to Hosea 8:8, what has happened to Israel?
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:8 says, 'Israel is swallowed up,' indicating their downfall.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 8:9 describes Ephraim as a wild ass alone by himself who has hired lovers.
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:9 says, 'Ephraim hath hired lovers,' and describes them as 'a wild ass alone by himself.'

questions.question: In Hosea 8, which comes first: Israel crying out 'My God, we know thee' or the statement about Israel casting off the good?
options: Israel crying out 'My God, we know thee'
Israel casting off the thing that is good
questions.correctAnswer: Israel crying out 'My God, we know thee'
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:2 has Israel crying out 'My God, we know thee' before Hosea 8:3 mentions casting off the good.

medium.title: Hosea Chapter 8 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Hosea Chapter 8 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Hosea 8:6, what is the origin of the calf of Samaria?
options: It was made by a workman, not by God
It was sent by God as a test
It appeared miraculously from the ground
It was inherited from the ancestors
questions.correctAnswer: It was made by a workman, not by God
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:6 states that the calf of Samaria was made by a workman and therefore is not God, emphasizing that it is a man-made idol and not divine.

questions.question: What does Hosea 8:7 mean by 'they have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind'?
options: Their actions will lead to severe consequences
Their crops will yield a great harvest
They will find peace and prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: Their actions will lead to severe consequences
questions.explanation: The metaphor in Hosea 8:7 indicates that Israel's sinful actions ('sowing the wind') will result in harsh judgment ('reaping the whirlwind'), showing a cause and effect of disobedience.

questions.question: How does Hosea 8:8 describe the fate of Israel among the Gentiles?
options: They shall be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure
They shall be leaders among the Gentiles
They shall be accepted and honored by the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:8 conveys that Israel will be swallowed up and treated with disdain among the Gentiles, like a vessel that is worthless and not pleasing.

questions.question: What imagery is used in Hosea 8:9 to describe Ephraim's alliance with Assyria?
options: A wild ass alone by himself
questions.correctAnswer: A wild ass alone by himself
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:9 uses the image of a wild ass alone to illustrate Ephraim's foolish and isolated alliance with Assyria, symbolizing instability and lack of guidance.

questions.question: Based on Hosea 8:10, what will God do despite Israel hiring among the nations?
options: Gather them and cause them to sorrow for their burden
Bless their alliances and protect them
Ignore their actions and remain silent
questions.correctAnswer: Gather them and cause them to sorrow for their burden
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:10 explains that although Israel has sought help among nations, God will gather them and they will experience sorrow due to the burden imposed by the king of princes.

questions.question: What lesson about trusting God can be drawn from the fact that Israel made kings not by God according to Hosea 8:4?
options: Trusting human authority without God's approval leads to downfall
Human kings are always better than divine guidance
God supports all human decisions unconditionally
questions.correctAnswer: Trusting human authority without God's approval leads to downfall
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:4 highlights that Israel appointed kings without God's knowledge, leading to idolatry and eventual judgment, teaching the importance of obedience to God's will in leadership.

questions.question: According to Hosea 8:11, how does Ephraim treat sin and altars?
options: They made many altars to sin, which became altars to sin for them
They destroyed all altars and repented
They worshipped only at the true altar of God
They built altars for peace and righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: They made many altars to sin, which became altars to sin for them
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:11 indicates that Ephraim's numerous altars were dedicated to sin, showing persistent disobedience and the resulting consequences of their actions.

questions.question: What does Hosea 8:12 say about Israel's response to God's law?
options: They counted God's law as a strange thing
They eagerly obeyed and treasured God's law
They wrote their own laws to replace God's
They taught God's law to the nations
questions.correctAnswer: They counted God's law as a strange thing
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:12 reveals that although God wrote great things of His law to Israel, they regarded it as something foreign and unacceptable, demonstrating rejection of divine guidance.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 8:13 states that the LORD accepted the sacrifices offered by Israel despite their sins.
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:13 clearly states that although Israel sacrificed flesh and ate it, the LORD did not accept these offerings and will remember their iniquity and sins.

questions.question: What consequence does Hosea 8:14 say will come upon Israel's cities and palaces?
options: A fire will be sent to devour them
They will be rebuilt with greater strength
They will be protected by angels
They will be given peace and prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: A fire will be sent to devour them
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:14 prophesies that God will send a fire upon Israel's cities which will consume the palaces, reflecting divine judgment for their sins.

questions.question: How does Hosea 8:7 connect to Hosea 8:8 in terms of the consequences of Israel's actions?
options: Sowing the wind leads to being swallowed up among the Gentiles
Sowing the wind leads to abundant harvest and peace
Being swallowed up among the Gentiles leads to sowing the wind
Sowing the wind leads to building strong cities
questions.correctAnswer: Sowing the wind leads to being swallowed up among the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:7 warns that their sinful actions ('sowing the wind') will produce destructive results ('reap the whirlwind'), and Hosea 8:8 describes this outcome as Israel being swallowed up and despised among Gentiles.

questions.question: If Israel continues to hire lovers among the nations as in Hosea 8:9, what does Hosea 8:10 say will happen?
options: God will gather them and they will sorrow for their burden
Their alliances will bring peace and safety
They will be exalted among the nations
They will receive God's full blessing
questions.correctAnswer: God will gather them and they will sorrow for their burden
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:10 shows that despite Israel's attempts to secure help by hiring foreign allies, God will gather them and bring sorrow as a consequence of their misplaced trust.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 8:2 indicates that Israel's cry to God is an expression of true knowledge and relationship.
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:2 records Israel crying to God and professing knowledge of Him, which reflects their recognition of God despite their disobedience.

questions.question: How does Hosea 8:5 illustrate God's anger towards Samaria?
options: The calf of Samaria has cast them off, provoking God's anger
Samaria repented and God showed mercy
God blessed Samaria for their faithfulness
Samaria was protected from all enemies
questions.correctAnswer: The calf of Samaria has cast them off, provoking God's anger
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:5 shows that the idol calf of Samaria has rejected the people, which incites God's anger and calls for their repentance.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 8:3 states that Israel has embraced what is good and will be safe from the enemy.
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:3 indicates that Israel has cast off what is good, and as a result, the enemy will pursue them, highlighting their vulnerability due to disobedience.

hard.title: Hosea Chapter 8 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Hosea Chapter 8.

questions.question: What consequence does Hosea 8:11 say will come upon Ephraim for making many altars to sin?
options: Altars shall be unto him to sin
He shall be blessed by the LORD
He will prosper in all his ways
He will be delivered from his enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Altars shall be unto him to sin
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:11 states that because Ephraim has made many altars to sin, altars shall be unto him to sin, indicating that their worship practices will bring judgment rather than blessing.

questions.question: According to Hosea 8:12, how did Israel treat the great things of God's law?
options: They counted them as a strange thing
They taught them to their children
questions.correctAnswer: They counted them as a strange thing
questions.explanation: In Hosea 8:12, God declares that though He wrote great things of His law to Israel, they regarded them as strange, showing their rejection and alienation from God's commands.

questions.question: What does Hosea 8:13 say about Israel’s sacrifices and the LORD’s acceptance of them?
options: The LORD is pleased with them
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:13 explains that Israel sacrifices flesh for offerings but eats it themselves, and the LORD does not accept these sacrifices, indicating their hypocrisy and disobedience.

questions.question: What punishment does Hosea 8:13 predict for Israel after the LORD remembers their iniquity?
options: They shall be exalted above nations
They shall dwell safely in their land
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:13 prophesies that after God remembers Israel's sins, they will return to Egypt, symbolizing exile or punishment reflecting their spiritual and political decline.

questions.question: According to Hosea 8:14, what has Israel forgotten, and what has Judah done in contrast?
options: Israel hath forgotten his Maker; Judah hath multiplied fenced cities
Israel hath worshipped idols; Judah hath repented
Israel hath built altars; Judah hath destroyed them
Israel hath kept the law; Judah hath forsaken it
questions.correctAnswer: Israel hath forgotten his Maker; Judah hath multiplied fenced cities
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:14 contrasts Israel's spiritual failure—forgetting God—with Judah’s focus on fortifying cities, highlighting different responses to crisis.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Hosea 8:7 with the phrase 'they have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind'?
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:7 uses metaphor to illustrate the cause and effect of Israel’s actions, implying that their reckless deeds (sowing the wind) will bring severe consequences (reaping the whirlwind). This metaphorical language warns of inevitable judgment.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of Israel forgetting their Maker as in Hosea 8:14?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:15 similarly describes Israel becoming 'fat, grown thick, and kicked'—forgetting their God—echoing Hosea 8:14’s theme of spiritual neglect leading to judgment.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the idea in Hosea 8:12 that God’s law was counted as a strange thing?
questions.explanation: John 1:11 states that the world did not recognize or receive Jesus, reflecting rejection similar to Israel counting God’s law as strange in Hosea 8:12.

questions.question: What is the significance of the Hebrew word translated as 'altars' in Hosea 8:11, and how does it relate to the chapter’s theme?
options: 'Mizbeach' meaning a place of sacrifice, indicating false worship
questions.correctAnswer: 'Mizbeach' meaning a place of sacrifice, indicating false worship
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'mizbeach' means altar, a place of sacrifice. In Hosea 8:11, multiple altars symbolize Israel’s proliferation of false worship sites, reinforcing the chapter’s theme of idolatry and sin.

questions.question: How does Hosea 8:9 use the metaphor of a 'wild ass alone by himself' to describe Israel's political situation?
options: Israel is isolated and reckless in seeking foreign alliances
Israel is protected by the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Israel is isolated and reckless in seeking foreign alliances
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:9 compares Israel to a wild ass alone, highlighting their isolation and impulsive political decisions, such as hiring 'lovers' (foreign allies), which leads to vulnerability.

questions.question: Which verse in Hosea 8 predicts that Israel's calf idol will be broken in pieces, and what does this symbolize?
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:6 states the calf of Samaria will be broken, symbolizing the coming judgment and destruction of Israel’s idolatry.

questions.question: What is the historical context behind Israel 'returning to Egypt' in Hosea 8:13?
options: It symbolizes exile and loss of freedom
It indicates literal return to Egypt for prosperity
It refers to a covenant renewal
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes exile and loss of freedom
questions.explanation: Returning to Egypt in Hosea 8:13 symbolizes exile and submission to foreign powers, indicating Israel’s loss of sovereignty as punishment for sin.

questions.question: Which theme in Hosea 8 anticipates the New Testament teaching on fruitfulness and consequences of sin seen in Galatians 6:7?
options: 'They have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind'
'Altars shall be unto him to sin'
'They sacrifice flesh for the sacrifices of mine offerings'
questions.correctAnswer: 'They have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind'
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:7’s metaphor about sowing and reaping parallels Galatians 6:7’s teaching that one reaps what they sow, emphasizing consequences for sin.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 8:10 indicates that although Israel has sought foreign allies, the LORD will gather them and they will experience sorrow.
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:10 shows God’s sovereignty in gathering Israel despite their reliance on foreign nations, with sorrow coming upon them for their disobedience.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 8:5 praises the calf of Samaria as a symbol of Israel's innocence and God's favor.
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:5 condemns the calf of Samaria, stating it has cast off Israel and kindled God's anger, opposing the idea of innocence or favor.

theological.title: Hosea Chapter 8 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Hosea Chapter 8 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Hosea 8:1 indicate about the coming judgment on Israel?
options: An eagle will come against them
A storm will pass over them
A flood will wash them away
questions.correctAnswer: An eagle will come against them
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:1 states that the Lord will come as an eagle against Israel due to their transgressions, indicating imminent judgment and divine intervention.

questions.question: According to Hosea 8:3, what has Israel done regarding good?
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:3 explicitly states that Israel has cast off the thing that is good, which leads to their impending destruction.

questions.question: What do the idols made from silver and gold represent in Hosea 8:4?
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:4 reveals that Israel set up princes and idols from their wealth, indicating a rebellion against God's authority.

questions.question: In Hosea 8:7, what is the consequence of sowing the wind?
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:7 warns that Israel's actions will lead to dire consequences, specifically that they will reap what they have sown, which is destruction.

questions.question: What does Hosea 8:10 say about Israel's alliances with other nations?
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:10 indicates that Israel's alliances will ultimately lead to sorrow, demonstrating the futility of relying on foreign powers.

questions.question: According to Hosea 8:11, what has Ephraim done regarding altars?
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:11 points out that Ephraim has constructed numerous altars for sin, which reflects their hardened hearts against God.

questions.question: What does Hosea 8:12 imply about Israel's attitude towards God's law?
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:12 states that the great things of God's law were counted as strange by Israel, signifying their rejection of divine instruction.

questions.question: What does Hosea 8:13 reveal about the sacrifices made by Israel?
options: They will be accepted by God
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:13 tells us that despite their sacrifices, the LORD does not accept them, indicating the futility of their worship due to unrepentant sin.

questions.question: In Hosea 8:14, what has Israel forgotten, leading to consequences?
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:14 highlights that Israel has forgotten their Maker, resulting in God's judgment and destruction of their cities.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight is derived from the combination of verses 5 and 6 regarding God's anger?
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 6 show that God's anger is directed towards Israel's idolatry, which ultimately leads to their destruction.

questions.question: What synthesis can be drawn from verses 10 and 11 about Israel's sin and its consequences?
options: Sin results in sorrow and judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Sin results in sorrow and judgment
questions.explanation: The combination of verses 10 and 11 indicates that Israel's sin, particularly through alliances and idolatry, will lead to sorrow and divine judgment.

questions.question: According to the synthesis of verses 2 and 8, what does Israel's cry signify?
questions.explanation: While Israel cries out to God, verse 8 indicates they are swallowed up and lack true repentance, revealing their false assurance.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that the God of the Old Testament is unjust in His wrath. What does Hosea 8:1-3 actually teach?
options: God's wrath is a response to sin
questions.correctAnswer: God's wrath is a response to sin
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:1-3 illustrates that God's judgment is a direct reaction to Israel's transgressions, emphasizing the just nature of His wrath towards sin.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted in Hosea 8:6 regarding the idols of Samaria?
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:6 shows that the idols made by man are not God; God's jealousy is evident as He desires exclusive worship from His people.

questions.question: What attribute of God does the judgment foretold in Hosea 8:14 reveal?
questions.explanation: Hosea 8:14 reveals that God's impending judgment on Israel's cities demonstrates His justice in response to their rebellion and idolatry.
